sections.label: Bill amends Act personal identifiers
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Act to allow ICA to collect more forms of personal identifiers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, the Bill amends the Act to allow ICA to collect more forms of personal identifiers.

sections.label: Minister sets out personal identifiers
sections.summary: Clause 2 lets the Minister set out in the Schedule the types of personal identifiers collectable under the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill allows the Minister to set out in the Schedule the types of personal identifiers that may be collected under the Act.

sections.label: Iris images collection from SCs PRs
sections.summary: ICA plans to start collecting iris images from SCs and PRs from next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: A new personal identifier we intend to collect are iris images.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: ICA plans to start collecting iris images from SCs and PRs from next year.

sections.label: Commissioner discretion to refuse names
sections.summary: The Commissioner may refuse registration of names resembling titles or awards, signifying lineage inconsistent with gender, or obscene, offensive or contrary to public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In addition to the mandatory rules, the Commissioner is given the discretion to refuse the registration of a name that: (a) contains anything that represents or resembles a title, a rank or an award, such as "Sir" or "Professor"; or (b) uses any expression or abbreviation to signify lineage, such as "bin" or "son of" or "daughter of", which does not correspond to the person's gender in the national register.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Commissioner is also given the discretion to refuse the registration of names which are obscene, offensive or contrary to public interest.

sections.label: Public officers as registration officers
sections.summary: Only public officers can be appointed as registration officers for certain enforcement and investigation powers under sections 15B, 16, 16B or 16C.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Only public officers can be appointed as registration officers for the purposes of certain enforcement and investigation related powers under sections 15B, 16, 16B or 16C.

sections.label: Enrol iris images during re-registration
sections.summary: One registration function is to enrol iris images during the NRIC re-registration process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: One such registration function is to enrol iris images during the NRIC re-registration process.

sections.label: Iris images for identity verification
sections.summary: A proposed amendment would collect iris images from citizens and permanent residents as an added identifier, and the MP asks how ICA would collect them from residents with mobility issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the proposed amendments is the collection of iris images from Singapore citizens and permanent residents as an additional identifier, to enhance the accuracy of identity verification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Developed countries, such as the US and the United Arab Emirates, have already adopted iris-scanning technology and it is timely that we do so, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask the Minister for Home Affairs to elaborate on how ICA would be collecting iris scans of our residents, particularly from those with mobility issues and are constrained to their homes due to ill health.

sections.label: Non-ICA employees as registration officers
sections.summary: Another proposed amendment is the appointment of non-ICA employees as registration officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another key proposed amendment is the appointment of non-ICA employees as registration officers.

sections.label: Cost of replacing lost NRIC
sections.summary: Existing rules, independent of the current Bill, set NRIC replacement at $100 for the first loss and $300 for the second loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the existing rules – and this is independent of the current Bill – are that replacing a lost NRIC costs $100 for the first loss and $300 for the second loss.

sections.label: NRIC replacement payment and name characters
sections.summary: The MP asks ICA to state that no one will be denied an NRIC replacement for inability to pay, and notes the 66-character name limit confirmed by the Senior Minister of State.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, can ICA publicly say or message that while certain penalties may apply on a case-by-case basis, no one will be denied an NRIC replacement because he cannot pay?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One of these rules is that the name cannot exceed the number of characters permitted by the electronic form of the national register, which the Senior Minister of State confirmed is 66 characters.

sections.label: Clause 14 new personal identifiers
sections.summary: Clause 14 lets the Minister collect new personal identifiers such as iris scans, and the MP seeks confirmation of intent to eventually migrate all Singaporeans and Permanent Residents to iris scan identification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 14 allows the Minister to collect new personal identifiers, such as an iris scan which reflects developments in personal identification technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would just like to confirm − I believe I heard this earlier − with the Senior Minister of State that the intention is for the Government to eventually migrate everyone, all Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, to this new iris scan identification and collection.

sections.label: Data intermediaries and national registration officer powers
sections.summary: The MP suggests MHA treat contracted organisations as data intermediaries under the PDPA, and notes an amendment giving national registration officers search, seizure and force powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To ensure a minimum standard of protection and reduce the compliance complexity for its outsourcers, I would like to suggest that MHA should, at the minimum, treat all organisations it is contracting with for the purpose of national registration, like data intermediaries, under the PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, the amendment to section 16(2A) allows a national registration officer to break open property, forcefully remove obstruction and take possession of documents found during a search.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This gives search, seizure and use of force powers to national registration officers, which the Senior Minister of State would confirm would be ICA officers only and not private sector persons, but, nevertheless, therefore, extending Police powers to another group of personnel outside of the Police.

sections.label: Bill explanatory note finances
sections.summary: The explanatory note to the Bill states that no extra financial expenditure would be entailed by the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The explanatory note to this Bill states that "no extra financial expenditure would be entailed by this Bill".

sections.label: Biometric data sharing examples
sections.summary: Brazil, NEC and a US official are cited on biometric data sharing, scanners and Singapore as a data registration model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Brazil has recently announced plans to share biometric data from their electoral registry with the federal government for a unified Brazilian identity card project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Japanese tech firm NEC has also developed new technology biometric scanners to identify even new-borns and infants to monitor vaccination rates in developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the Straits Times on 5 November, it was also pointed out by a senior cybersecurity official of the US Office of the Director of National Intelligence that Singapore can be a model for building a resilient national critical information infrastructure with regard to national data registration.

sections.label: One-time registration exercise question
sections.summary: A member asks whether the Ministry would consider a one-time exercise to register all citizens quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My clarification is, if this was an important part of our security and national registration framework, would the Ministry not consider that this be done as a one-time exercise to allow for all citizens to be registered as quickly as possible?

sections.label: Clause 14 personal identifiers
sections.summary: Clause 14 inserts a Schedule listing the personal identifiers that may be collected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A significant amendment is clause 14 which inserts a Schedule, including the personal identifiers that may be collected.

sections.label: Iris recognition concerns
sections.summary: Countries use iris technology, but studies show cataract surgery may affect iris recognition and synthetic eye images are a concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Due to these advantages, several countries, such as the UK, the Netherlands and India, are using this technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There have been studies that showed that cataract surgeries could change the iris texture and may impact iris pattern recognition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another concern is the possibility of recreating synthetic eye images that match digital iris codes used by iris-recognition systems to identify people.

sections.label: Inappropriate names and iris scans
sections.summary: The Bill refuses inappropriate names, expands personal identifiers collected by ICA, and may collect iris scans from citizens and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, the move to refuse the registration of inappropriate names is overdue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is particularly important to reject misleading and confusing names which can be used to deceive the general public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to amend the Act to expand types of personal identifiers of persons registered or required to be registered under the Act that may be collected by ICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The collection of iris scans from Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents could begin as early as next year, according to ICA, as an extra personal identifier, besides photographs and fingerprints.

sections.label: Iris scan distance
sections.summary: Iris scan technology can be taken from as far as 12 m away, according to publicly highlighted scientific sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Iris scan technology can be taken from as far as 12 m away, according to scientific sources highlighted publicly.

sections.label: NRIC renewal and re-issuance
sections.summary: He reiterates the need for ICA to renew and re-issue NRICs in later years and at selected intervals because NRIC pictures may be outdated and inaccurate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: On a different note and point but also on the National Registration Identification system, I had raised previously as a Parliamentary Question earlier this year but reiterate again the need for ICA to renew and re-issue our NRICs again during the later years of our life and at selected intervals because the pictures on the NRIC may be outdated and inaccurate.

sections.label: Iris scans complement fingerprints
sections.summary: Iris scans will complement fingerprint matching at immigration clearance, giving ICA another way to verify identity and letting travellers use iris scans instead of manned counters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: He also asked if iris scans will eventually replace current fingerprint verification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This will complement the current fingerprint matching process at immigration clearance and give ICA another way to verify a traveller's identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Travellers using the automatic clearance lanes who find that their fingerprints cannot be matched, can also use iris scans, instead of being re-directed to manned counters.

sections.label: Iris enrolment at collection
sections.summary: ICA will enrol an individual's iris images when he collects his new NRIC or passport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: ICA will enrol an individual's iris images when he collects his new NRIC or passport.

sections.label: Iris pattern stability
sections.summary: Based on US National Institutes of Standards and Technology reports, iris patterns are relatively stable over time and have lower mismatch rates than other biometric identifiers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on reports by the National Institutes of Standards and Technology of the US Department of Commerce, iris patterns are relatively stable over time Page: 46 and have lower mismatch rates, as compared to other biometric identifiers.

sections.label: Limiting enrolment to existing interfaces
sections.summary: To minimise inconvenience to the public, enrolment is limited to interfaces ICA already has with the public: registration at 15 and re-registration in subsequent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: At this point in time, in order to minimise inconvenience to members of the public, we are limiting enrolment to those interfaces that ICA already has with members of the public ‒ registration at 15, and re-registration in subsequent years.

sections.label: ICA officers' functions and limits
sections.summary: These officers may issue NRICs and enrol iris images but will not perform sensitive functions accessing personal information in ICA records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These may include functions, such as the issuance of NRICs and enrolling of iris images.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They will not be appointed to perform sensitive functions that require them to access, retrieve or alter individuals' personal information in ICA's records.

sections.label: Officers deemed public servants
sections.summary: Under a new section 3A, officers and individuals appointed by the Commissioner of ICA are deemed public servants under the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In addition, under a new section 3A, these officers and individuals who are appointed by the Commissioner of ICA will be deemed to be public servants for the purposes of the Penal Code.

sections.label: No guidelines on allowable names
sections.summary: ICA does not intend to prescribe guidelines on allowable names since the vast majority of names are registered without issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: ICA does not intend to prescribe a set of guidelines on allowable names, since the vast majority of names are registered without issue.

sections.label: Waiving IC replacement fees
sections.summary: ICA will consider fully or partially waiving replacement fees where IC loss was not through negligence, such as theft or financial difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: ICA will consider waiving the replacement fees fully or partially for cases where the loss of IC was not through negligence but due to circumstances beyond the cardholder's control, for example, their wallet was stolen or they faced financial difficulties.

sections.label: NRIC re-registration and name denials
sections.summary: A person registers a first NRIC at 15 and a second at 30; ICA is looking at another re-registration later, and the Bill will not increase public expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In relation to Mr Patrick Tay's earlier question, currently, a person registers and receives his first NRIC at the age of 15 and he then has to re-register to receive a second NRIC at 30, with an updated photograph.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: ICA is looking at introducing another NRIC re-registration at a later phase of a cardholder's life so that the information captured, such as the photograph, will be more up-to-date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The enactment of the Bill and its execution will not cause an increase in public expenditure itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Just a quick point of clarification on the denial of registration of impermissible names because of character limit or other reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that this is very rare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Would the Senior Minister of State be able to share with us his broad ballpark estimate, based on the number of cases ICA has seen of the number of names that are likely not to be approved to be registered each year under these new rules, very broadly speaking?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Suffice to say, as I have said earlier, these are few and far between.
